chapters.subtitle: From the grower's phone to the grower's reward
intro: This page follows one capture through the Greenstand system. A capture is one photo of a tree, with its GPS point and some data. A grower takes it with the Treetracker app.
Chapter 1 follows the capture from the grower's phone to the grower's reward. This page says "grower". Older code and tables say "planter" for the same person.

stages.title: On the phone: the grower takes a capture
story: The grower opens the Treetracker app on an Android phone. On the first day, the grower signs up with a name, a phone number or an email, and a selfie. On later days, the grower picks a name from a list on the phone.

The grower walks to a young tree and taps TRACK. The app waits until the GPS point is stable. The grower takes a photo of the tree, checks it, and can add a note. The app keeps the photo and the GPS point on the phone, so the grower needs no network.

stages.title: The upload: from the phone to cloud storage
story: Later, in a place with internet, the grower taps UPLOAD. The app sends each photo to cloud storage. Then it sends a small data file, a "bundle". A bundle lists up to 50 captures: where, when, and which photo.
The app then marks each capture as uploaded and deletes the photo from the phone.

stages.title: The bundle chain: four small services open the bundle
story: Cloud storage tells a small Greenstand service that a new bundle arrives. That service keeps the bundle. Every 5 minutes, a second service opens the new bundles. A third service passes each capture on to the service that stores it. A fourth service, the older path, also gets each capture. It stores the older tree record itself, if that record is not there yet.
These four services are public Greenstand repos. They are not in the docs repo yet, so they have no viewer.

stages.title: The record: the capture waits for verification
story: The field data service stores the capture as a "raw capture" with the status "unprocessed". The capture now waits for verification.
On the public web map, the page of the tree can already show the badge "Waiting for verification".

stages.title: Verification: an admin checks the photo
story: An admin signs in to the admin panel and opens the Verify page. The page shows a grid of photos that wait for verification. The admin looks at each photo.

The admin approves the photo, with the type of planting, the age of the tree, and the species if the admin knows it. Or the admin rejects it, with a reason, for example "Not a tree" or "Blurry photo". On the web map, an approved capture shows "Verified". A rejected capture is not active any more, so the map hides it.

stages.title: The reward: the grower earns money
story: In the code, one organization has a payment rule. Every day, an automatic job counts the approved captures of each of its growers. It pays in steps of 100 captures: 100 captures give 120,000 leones, and 1,000 captures or more give the maximum, 1,200,000 leones. The job writes an "earning" with the status "calculated".

Greenstand's guide to earnings and payments gives the next steps for a typical case. In that case, a funder does them. A funder is the person or the organization that pays for the captures. The funder opens the Earnings page of the admin panel and downloads the list. Then the funder pays each grower outside the Greenstand system. Last, the funder logs the payments. The funder logs one earning in its detail panel, or many earnings with a file upload on the Payments page. Each logged earning becomes "paid". The guide says that the growers can see the payment data. But the Treetracker app and the wallet app have no earnings screen. So the grower learns about the money from the payment itself.

flags.text: The organization is FCC, which we think is Freetown City Council. The job and the payments still run today. (The code shows no change since 2023.)
flags.question: Is FCC the Freetown City Council, does the daily FCC earnings job still run, and do the funders still pay the growers and log the payments this way?

flags.text: The wallet app tells each new user "we will gift you 1 token". The token does not arrive today.

stages.note: Tokens are not a grower reward today. An operator can start a job that puts one token for each approved capture of an organization's growers into a wallet that the operator names. Greenstand's white paper describes a goal, not the code of today. In that goal, each capture becomes a token in the wallet of the entity that is responsible for the tree. When claims conflict, the grower comes first. The token also holds a proof of the payment to the grower. The token job of today does not use the wallet of the grower, and no token holds payment data. Chapter 3, the impact token, will tell that story.

chapters.subtitle: The capture on the public web map
intro: This chapter follows one capture onto the public web map, map.treetracker.org. Anyone can open the map and see the trees that growers captured.
The web map shows a capture in two ways: close up as a pin, and from further away as a part of the number on a cluster. A click on a pin opens the tree page.

stages.title: The pin: the capture is on the map before verification
story: When the field data service stores the capture (chapter 1, stage 4), the database also keeps an older tree record of it. This record is "active" at once. It is not "approved" yet.

The map is a set of small square images, the tiles. The browser asks the tile server for each tile. The mark "active" shows a capture on the map. So close up, the new capture is a pin at once, before an admin verifies it.
stages.note: Greenstand's product page says that the web map shows verified trees. Today, the map shows each active capture, also before verification.

stages.title: The clusters: a job adds the capture to the counts
story: From further away, the map groups the captures into round clusters. A cluster shows a number: the count of its captures.

An automatic job is set to run every 2 hours. It finds the active captures that are not in a cluster yet. Then it builds the clusters again. Until the next run, the new capture is a pin close up. It is not in the counts yet.

stages.title: The approval: only the tree page changes
story: An admin approves the capture (chapter 1, stage 5). The admin panel saves "approved" in the record. It also saves the age of the tree, the type of planting, and the species if the admin knows it. Nothing sends a message to the map. The pin and the counts stay the same.
Only the tree page changes. Its badge "Waiting for verification" becomes "Verified". If the admin rejects the capture, the record is not active any more. Then the map hides it.

stages.title: The tree page: what a visitor sees
story: A visitor clicks a pin. The web map opens the tree page beside the map. The page shows the photo, the tree number, the badges, the date of the capture, the country, and the species. The photo comes straight from cloud storage.
The web map keeps each tree page for a time before it builds the page again. So "Verified" can show hours after the approval.
